analysis: The supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 3291-3699), historical release notes. The patch changes only CHANGELOG.md (head 11-400, a new v0.10.9 candidate section with upgrade and rollout notes). The visible patch excerpt is truncated; it holds only documentation text. The BASE units contain no executable code, configuration, or security control. No source files, wire contracts, or threat-model definitions are modified in the supplied evidence, so I found no regression against TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, TB-012, T-041, or other defined threats. The changelog restates existing accepted-risk context such as SEC-035 and the T-041 30-minute SSD TTL, and describes already-reviewed behavior. I did not treat these as new issues. The patch notes advise operators on pair upgrades and `darkbloom stop --solo` and `--forget` usage. They are operational guidance only and do not alter authorization, attestation, encryption or billing controls. The patch excerpt is truncated at line ~25 of the new section, so the remaining ~375 added head lines were not visible. Those later lines may describe code changes in other files, such as cluster pairing, GPU limit (TB-014/T-062), and add-on hold (TB-012), that a different batch should review. Nothing in these units establishes that any such change is safe or unsafe; the changelog itself is not evidence of the actual behavior. Integration should check whether the code changes for 0.10.9 match the threat-model boundaries, particularly pair-member registration and solo-serving locks (A-018, T-059).
